analysis:
Documentation-only PR: docs/consumer/verification.md (head text, lines 1-280) and docs/developer/build.md (patch adding a paragraph near line 1102 on the default-off supervised App Attest worker candidate). No code, config, or security-control changes were visible. The one coverage limit is that the build.md patch is against a file much longer than the supplied base excerpt (base shown only to line ~446); I examined the hunk but not its surroundings. Unit 9258958b65ed8e68:0 is metadata only.

Security-relevant claims in the docs, checked against TB-002, TB-009 and the TB-011/T-052..T-058 summaries:
- verification.md line 25-31: the worker candidate keeps the endpoint private key in the parent, uses bounded IPC between the same-signed-executable child and parent, adds no verification bypass, and changes no proof or authorization lifetime. It is described as default-off (DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION=1) and not production-qualified. This is consistent with A-003/A-015/A-016 and the TB-011 assumptions, so no assumption is invalidated. The next pass should confirm that the implementing code actually keeps the key in the parent and retires stuck workers; this PR does not supply that code.
- verification.md line 72-77: the endpoint-resumption candidate extends no Apple proof lifetime and is not a consumer-verifiable credential. This matches the canonical header comments.
- build.md: the new paragraph says the worker opt-in also reaches background serving through the saved LaunchAgent plist, and that diagnostic/fault flags are not forwarded. This is a notable operational expansion of the env opt-in surface (T-052/T-053). It is documented only, and the worker is not claimed to be qualified. A later code pass should check that the plist forwarding cannot be abused by a local operator to enable unqualified paths. A local operator is already adversarial under ADV-001/TB-003 and still faces coordinator-side proof verification and final-dispatch authorization checks.
- The build.md paragraph points to sibling darkbloom-platform for the native verifier and backend docs, consistent with the platform-owned policy split noted in the context.

No findings. The threat model does not need updating for the docs alone; if the worker candidate code lands, consider adding it to TB-011/T-053 scope.
